summary.text: The supremacy of knowledge raises a practical question: how does a seeker approach it? The teacher explains ego-surrender, comprehensive sincere questioning and sustained service as complementary aspects of discipleship. A teacher needs both scriptural means of communication and direct recognition of truth. Instruction redirects attention toward the innermost subject rather than supplying another object of knowledge. The next verse promises an end to delusion and a positive vision of all beings in Atma and in Krishna. These are explained as two perspectives on one nondual recognition; the teacher explicitly leaves the explanation unfinished.

segments.heading: The seeker asks how knowledge is approached

blocks.text: The next teaching answers how to approach the knowledge in which action culminates. The guru-disciple relationship is presented as its living vehicle.
Pranipata means more than bodily prostration: surrender the ego's claims to superior understanding, incompleteness and agency so the teaching can be received rather than defended against.

segments.heading: Questioning is active reflection, not contest

blocks.text: Pariprasna examines doubt and misunderstanding from every side. The teacher distinguishes this inquiry from trying to defeat, test or find fault with the teacher.
A declaration alone cannot do the student's reflecting. Voicing objections and receiving clarification makes manana interactive until uncertainty is removed.
Seva is sustained, willing participation rather than hired labor. Daily proximity offers occasions to see the teaching embodied and to relinquish ego through ordinary responsibilities.

Together surrender, questioning and service express the disciple's preparation. The promise of instruction is explained conditionally: genuine receptivity meets a teacher who points toward directly seeing Atma.

segments.heading: The teacher needs learning and direct recognition

blocks.text: Scriptural expertise supplies content and reasoning, but alone does not establish direct recognition. Conversely, experience without communicative tools may fail to guide another person.
The ideal combines learned exposition with living establishment in truth. The teacher connects this pairing with the Upanishadic description of a qualified guru.

segments.heading: Instruction turns attention toward the subject

blocks.text: Independent study can remain indirect because Atma is the knowing subject, not another object. The guru's pointing redirects attention toward what was always present.
The commentary's sample questions concern bondage, release, knowledge and ignorance. It stresses the effectiveness of instruction grounded in truth rather than mere verbal learning.
Moha includes confusing body with self, agent with non-agent, and transient things with permanence. Arjuna's paralysis illustrates the practical force of this confusion.
The promised non-return of delusion rests on sublation rather than temporary suppression. The bodily identification is recognized as a superimposition instead of being treated as reality.

segments.heading: All beings in Atma and in Krishna

blocks.text: The positive side of the same knowledge is seeing every being within Atma. Forms continue to appear, but no longer as realities independent of consciousness.
Seeing beings in oneself and in Krishna discloses the identity of inward self and Brahman from complementary directions. The teacher says further explanation is needed and postpones completion.

concepts.label: Pranipata
concepts.gloss: Surrender of the ego that makes discipleship receptive.

concepts.label: Pariprasna
concepts.gloss: Sincere, comprehensive questioning that voices reflection.

concepts.label: Seva
concepts.gloss: Continuous service and proximity renewing surrender.

concepts.label: Tattva darshi
concepts.gloss: A teacher who has directly recognized truth.

concepts.label: Prathyagatma
concepts.gloss: The innermost subject, not an ordinary object of cognition.

concepts.label: Moha
concepts.gloss: Confusion of self with body, agency and impermanence.

concepts.label: Sarvat Mahava
concepts.gloss: The inclusive vision of Brahman without excluding any being.
